title: Herod's death year and the census of Quirinius: what the primary evidence supports for the Chronomap's birth chronology
question: What do Josephus (Ant. 17-18), the candidate lunar eclipses of 15/16 September 5 BCE, 12/13 March 4 BCE and 10 January 1 BCE, Herodian and successor numismatics, the Titulus Tiburtinus (CIL XIV 3613), the Q. Aemilius Secundus inscription (CIL III 6687) and current peer-reviewed Herodian chronology establish about the year of Herod the Great's death and the date and status of the Quirinius census, and which statements can be labelled [A]/[R], [S] or [T]? Specifically: does the 4 BCE eclipse satisfy Josephus' sequence (eclipse, Antipater's execution five days later, Herod's death, a Passover); what are the strongest arguments for 5 or 1 BCE; is the 'second legateship' of Quirinius in Syria epigraphically established or only inferred; and how should the Chronomap present its two birth axes (before Herod's death versus the 6 CE census) without turning a contested chronology into a settled date?
why_now: Chronomap Jesus chapter 01 (docs/world/chronomap-jesus/01-geburt-und-volkszaehlung.md, header revised 12/23.11.2026) makes Herod's death year the first switch of the whole chronology and lists 4, 5 and 1 BCE alongside the Quirinius problem; the person-and-place rollout for chapters 02-03 is queued for 24.11.2026, so the birth axis will be propagated into more files.
real_world_anchor: The year of Herod the Great's death and the census of Quirinius: Josephus Ant. 17-18, the 5/4/1 BCE lunar-eclipse candidates, the Titulus Tiburtinus (CIL XIV 3613), and Herodian and successor numismatics.
novelty_reason: The queued Passion-chronology topic covers the crucifixion between 26 and 36 CE (Passover weekdays, the reported darkness, and the 3 April 33 lunar eclipse). It does not examine Herod's death in 5/4/1 BCE, the Herodian succession and numismatics, the Titulus Tiburtinus, or the 6 CE Quirinius census that form the birth chronology. This gap adds the BCE/CE birth axis and does not repeat the Passion question.
